title: Remote monitoring after cardiac surgery across four centres: a cohort study of readmission and cost
abstract: Objective: to estimate the effect of remote monitoring after cardiac surgery on 30-day readmission and 90-day cost, and the cost per readmission avoided. Design: four-centre cohort from provincial data, 2023 to 2026, with before-and-after contrasts between adopting and comparison centres. Results will follow analysis.
introduction: Remote monitoring after surgery may prevent readmissions, but estimates are imprecise and economic models borrow them.
methods: Provincial discharge abstracts, billing and platform logs; difference-in-differences with case-mix adjustment; wild cluster bootstrap; centre C's comparison period ends at its pilot.
results: No data have been analysed yet.
discussion: The discussion will set the estimate against the trial and review and explain what the four-centre design can and cannot show.
limitations: Four centres; non-random adoption; missing home care and medication costs.
reportingChecklist: STROBE with RECORD; CHEERS 2022 for the cost analysis
summary: Cohort report structure with results left empty.
